痘.meaning: A farmer stores sacks of <part>beans</part> in a <part>leaky shed</part>. One stormy night the drips soak them, and they swell and burst like popcorn, sticking all over the cow sleeping inside. By morning she's covered in little round bumps, as if she's caught the <kanji>pox</kanji>.
痘.on: The last bean pings off the farmer's bare <sound>toe</sound> as he opens the door.

儒.meaning: At a rowdy tea house, customers <part>demand</part> faster service. The calm old waiter hangs his apron on a <part>coat hook</part>, bows, and serves each one a cup with a wise saying about patience and respecting your elders. The rudest customer bows back. The whole tea house turns <kanji>Confucian</kanji>.
儒.on: Soon a whole <sound>ju</sound>ry of customers sits in silence, sipping and nodding.

窃.meaning: A badger burglar never uses the door. From the cellar he <part>cut</part>s a neat round <part>hole</part> up through the cheese shop floor, lifts out one wheel of cheese and slides the plug back. Nobody hears a thing: pure <kanji>stealth</kanji>.
窃.on: Only the shop's <sound>set</sound>ter dog sniffs the floor and lifts one ear.
窃.kun: He hides the cheese in a <sound>noo</sound>k behind the chimney, among the <sound>soo</sound>t.

矯.meaning: After an earthquake, a <part>skyscraper</part> leans like a tired giraffe. An engineer fires a <part>dart</part> trailing a steel cable into its top floor, and the whole city grabs the rope and pulls, inch by inch, until it stands straight again: they <kanji>rectify</kanji> it.
矯.on: A lost tourist leans out of the top window and calls, '<sound>Kyo</sound>to?', holding the first part long, as if the tower might answer.
矯.kun: When it's done, the engineer takes a bow on the <sound>ta</sound>rmac.

醒.meaning: A falling <part>star</part> lands on a stick of <part>dynamite</part> beside a snoring night guard. BOOM: it was packed with confetti, and the guard sits bolt upright, eyes like saucers. He has never been so <kanji>awake</kanji>.
醒.on: He checks the steel <sound>sa</sound>fe he was meant to be guarding: still locked.
醒.kun: His neighbour runs over in her <sound>sa</sound>ri to shake the rest of the confetti off him.

喝.meaning: A lifeguard sits under a <part>sunshade</part> all day, shouting from her <part>mouth</part> at swimmers: 'Too far! Come back! No running!' By sunset, all that comes out is a tiny croak, and a seagull has to shout for her. Her voice is <kanji>hoarse</kanji>.
喝.on: A swimmer brings her a hot <sound>katsu</sound> sandwich, and she can only croak her thanks.

岬.meaning: A <part>mountain</part> wades out into the sea wearing a shell of <part>armor</part> on its nose, to take the hits from the waves. The fishing town shelters behind it. Sailors call that rocky point a <kanji>headland</kanji>.
岬.on: On its tip stands a lighthouse shaped like an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
岬.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>!' barks a seal, claiming the tip, and lines up its <sound>sar</sound>dines next to a stolen <sound>ki</sound>wi.

彙.meaning: A fussy hedgehog presses his <part>blanket</part> flat with a tiny <part>iron</part>, then tips out a basket of <part>fruit</part> and sorts it: apples in one row, plums in another, never mixed. Every row holds things of the <kanji>same kind</kanji>.
彙.on: A visiting <sound>ee</sound>l tries to wriggle into the plum row and is gently sent back.
彙.kun: At bedtime the hedgehog sighs '<sound>Ha</sound>,' fluffs up his <sound>ree</sound>d <sound>ne</sound>st, rests his head on a <sound>zu</sound>cchini and murmurs, 'Just <sound>me</sound>.'

綻.meaning: A tailor is <part>determine</part>d to fit a giant into a suit sewn with ordinary <part>thread</part>. The giant takes one deep breath, and every seam pops at once until the jacket hangs in rags. Cloth pulled that tight is bound to <kanji>be rent</kanji>.
綻.on: His shirt tail flaps like a windsock as he stomps off into a <sound>tun</sound>nel.
綻.kun: On the far side the giant just smiles and naps in the <sound>ho</sound>t sun, on a camp <sound>co</sound>t propped on a <sound>ro</sound>ck.

拷.meaning: A pirate captain drops <part>anchor</part> in a dead-calm sea and makes his crew <part>consider</part> his poetry: all nine hundred verses, read aloud very slowly. Nobody may leave the deck until the end. For the crew, it's sheer <kanji>torture</kanji>.
拷.on: Even the ship's <sound>goa</sound>t covers its ears with its hooves.

弄.meaning: A bored <part>king</part> sets up a <part>goal</part> in the palace garden and spends the afternoon kicking his crown into it, juggling his sceptre and twirling his robe tassels. Ruling can wait: he'd rather <kanji>play with</kanji> things.
弄.on: His goalkeeper is a red <sound>ro</sound>se in a flowerpot.
弄.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' cries the queen, as he twiddles every knob on the royal <sound>jee</sound>p.

崖.meaning: Miners dig a <part>quarry</part> into the side of a <part>mountain</part> and keep cutting straight down, year after year. One morning they peer over the edge and see a sheer wall of rock dropping away into the clouds: a <kanji>cliff</kanji>.
崖.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog leads them safely back from the edge.
崖.kun: A stone <sound>gar</sound>goyle perched on the rim keeps their <sound>ke</sound>ttle warm.

酎.meaning: A golfer hides a bottle in a crate stamped <part>dynamite</part> so nobody pinches it. After eighteen holes he prises the lid off with his <part>golf club</part>, and the clear spirit inside is so strong his cap flies off at the first sniff: <kanji>shochu</kanji>.
酎.on: He chases the taste with a stick of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum.
酎.kun: His caddie mixes the next batch in the back of the golf <sound>car</sound>t, stirring it with a <sound>mo</sound>p: to brew.

坪.meaning: Two cats both want the sunniest spot in the garden. The gardener rakes one square of <part>soil</part> perfectly <part>flat</part>, just big enough for two sleeping mats side by side, and the cats share it. That snug square is one <kanji>tsubo</kanji>.
坪.on: She tops each mat with a soft pile of <sound>hay</sound>.
坪.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes one cat in the hay, and knocks a milk <sound>bo</sound>ttle off the wall.

蹴.meaning: A referee starts reading a long rule <part>concerning</part> who may touch the ball. The goalkeeper isn't listening: he plants his left <part>foot</part>, swings the right, and sends the rulebook sailing over the stand. That's a <kanji>kick</kanji>.
蹴.on: Out of the book falls a <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be the referee was saving, and a pigeon catches it.
蹴.kun: The pigeon dips it in <sound>ke</sound>tchup before swallowing it.

享.meaning: A <part>child</part> lifts the <part>lid</part> of Grandma's sewing tin expecting buttons, and finds it packed with chocolates. One goes in her <part>mouth</part>, then another; she lies back on the rug and does nothing but <kanji>enjoy</kanji>.
享.on: The tin has a faded picture of <sound>Kyo</sound>to on it, and Grandma, coming in, says the name dreamily, stretching its start: 'Kyooo-to.'
享.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>h,' she says, as Grandma drops one more into her hand.

餅.meaning: At a picnic beside the <part>rugby posts</part>, a cook pounds rice into a soft white <part>food</part> so stretchy that a kicker pulls it all the way from one post to the other, like a sticky goal net. It's a rice cake: <kanji>mochi</kanji>.
餅.on: The players tumble into a pile of <sound>hay</sound>, laughing, dusted white.
餅.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>th lands on the sticky net, then flutters off onto the kicker's <sound>chee</sound>k.

柿.meaning: Each autumn the oldest <part>tree</part> in town runs its own <part>market</part> stall, dropping bright orange fruit straight into shoppers' baskets: bitter if you're rude, honey-sweet if you say please. The whole town learns manners for a <kanji>persimmon</kanji>.
柿.on: A knight queues politely, holding out his <sound>shie</sound>ld as a basket.
柿.kun: His squire shakes a branch with a <sound>ka</sound>rate chop, and down drops one persimmon and a startled <sound>ki</sound>wi bird.

吟.meaning: A poet on a train opens her <part>mouth</part> whenever anything happens: a cow, a tunnel, a sneeze. She turns each moment into a rhyme right <part>now</part>, on the spot. The other passengers groan, but she can't help it: she has to <kanji>versify</kanji>.
吟.on: 'Let the recital be<sound>gin</sound>!' calls the conductor, and she turns that into a rhyme too.

溺.meaning: A paper boat with a <part>weak</part> little sail bobs down the gutter. The rain gets heavier, <part>water drops</part> pile into it one by one, and slowly it tips, fills and slips under. The poor boat starts to <kanji>drown</kanji>.
溺.on: The frog riding on its <sound>de</sound>ck leaps to the kerb with its packed lunch: one <sound>ki</sound>wi.
溺.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter fishes the boat out and dries it by a <sound>bo</sound>nfire.

戴.meaning: A guard plants his <part>halberd</part> in the town square with a crown balanced on its tip. Each spring a <part>different</part> farmer gets to wear the crown for a day, and the whole town cheerfully agrees to <kanji>live under</kanji> them.
戴.on: The new ruler always gets a silk <sound>tie</sound> with the crown.
戴.kun: This year an <sound>ee</sound>l farmer wins: '<sound>Ta</sound>-<sound>da</sound>!' he sings, bowing low to receive it.

嗅.meaning: At a cheese contest, the judge refuses to taste anything. She holds each <part>stinking</part> wedge under her nose, keeps her <part>mouth</part> shut tight, takes one long, slow sniff, and gives her score. Her whole job is to <kanji>smell</kanji>.
嗅.on: She points at the winner with a pool <sound>cue</sound>, from a safe distance.
嗅.kun: The runner-up is a blue cheese so ripe she sniffs it from inside her <sound>car</sound>.

顎.meaning: A toymaker gives a <part>rubber duck</part> a wooden <part>nutcracker</part> mouth. Now it floats round the bath cracking walnuts, its hinged chin snapping open and shut: the duck with the iron <kanji>jaw</kanji>.
顎.on: A <sound>gag</sound>gle of geese queues at the tub, each holding a walnut.
顎.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' says the dentist, peering at its jaw through her <sound>go</sound>ggles.

傲.meaning: A man once <part>set free</part> a ladybird from a jam jar. Now he's built a statue of himself on a mound of <part>soil</part> at the spot, with his best hat on a <part>coat hook</part> beside it for visitors to admire. He's decided to <kanji>be proud</kanji> forever.
傲.on: Every morning he makes the neighbour's <sound>goa</sound>t bow to the statue.
傲.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter rolls its eyes and <sound>go</sound>bbles his sandwich.

凄.meaning: Every night at three, the teapot in the kitchen freezes solid. A <part>wife</part> stays up to watch: no draught, no open window, yet <part>ice</part> creeps up the spout and the cups rattle in their saucers on their own. She tiptoes back to bed with goosebumps. Something here is <kanji>uncanny</kanji>.
凄.on: Her husband locks the frozen teapot in a <sound>sa</sound>fe, just in case.
凄.kun: Frost settles like <sound>soo</sound>t on the window, and he whispers, '<sound>Go</sound>sh.'

蜂.meaning: An <part>insect</part> sits on top of a tiny <part>lookout post</part> in the clover field, watching for clouds. When rain is coming she buzzes the alarm, and every worker flies home with full baskets of pollen. She's the lookout <kanji>bee</kanji>.
蜂.on: When the farmer waters the field with a <sound>ho</sound>se, she sounds the alarm by mistake.
蜂.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the farmer, and says sorry with a drop of honey on a <sound>chee</sound>se cracker.

裾.meaning: A tailor who <part>reside</part>s at the top of a windy tower hangs his trousers on the <part>weathervane</part> to dry. They spin all night and fray at the ends, so every morning he folds and stitches the bottom of each leg again: a fresh <kanji>cuff</kanji>.
裾.on: He buys his thread from a little street <sound>kio</sound>sk at the foot of the tower.
裾.kun: The kiosk owner pays him for the mending in <sound>su</sound>shi and one odd <sound>so</sound>ck.

頓.meaning: A <part>rubber duck</part> is tied to a <part>hitching post</part> outside the saloon like a horse, and all day it sits there quietly. Then someone upstairs starts running a bath, and <kanji>suddenly</kanji> it snaps its rope and is gone.
頓.on: The barman fishes it out of the tub with a pair of <sound>ton</sound>gs.
頓.kun: The old cowboy on the porch drops his darning <sound>nee</sound>dle, cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!' and leaps into his <sound>car</sound> to give chase.

梗.meaning: At sunset the <part>night watch</part> walks his round past the oldest <part>tree</part> in the park, and the tree lowers its branches across the gate, knitting them tight. Nobody gets in until dawn: the tree helps the guard <kanji>close up</kanji>.
梗.on: A late visitor pokes an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne through the twigs, but even that won't fit.
梗.kun: The guard settles on a <sound>fu</sound>ton by the blocked gate with a long <sound>sa</sound>ga to read, and pats the trunk: '<sound>Goo</sound>d tree.'

姻.meaning: A <part>woman</part> marches every week for her <part>cause</part>: saving the town's old bandstand. A man with the same banner marches beside her, rain or shine. A year later they hold their wedding in that bandstand: <kanji>matrimony</kanji>.
姻.on: They sign the register with the same pot of <sound>in</sound>k they used for their banners.
